description: Figure 8(d) illustrates the performance of knowledge probing on the Qwen2.5 model after applying different editing methods. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is plotted on a logarithmic scale, ranging from $10^0$ to $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)," represents the accuracy in percentage and ranges from 60% to 80%. The plot displays five distinct lines, each corresponding to a different method: "Base" (black, solid line with circle markers), "FT" (blue, dashed line with triangle markers), "MEND" (brown, dash-dotted line with square markers), "MEMIT" (purple, dotted line with diamond markers), and "ROME" (green, solid line with square markers). All five lines show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases. The "ROME" method consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 75% and rising to about 81%. The "MEMIT" method follows, starting at around 70% and reaching approximately 78%. The "MEND" method starts at about 70% and increases to roughly 79%. The "FT" method begins at approximately 67% and reaches about 74%. The "Base" method, representing the model without editing, starts at about 65% and increases to approximately 72%.
